# 4. Read In Raw Counts
```{r READ-COUNTS, message=FALSE}
#------------------------ 4.1 LOAD GENOME ALIGNMENT FILES ------------------------# 
featcount <- read_tsv("./Data_Repository/Log2ABA.featcount.txt", skip = 1)
count_cols <- colnames(featcount)[7:ncol(featcount)] # backup OG names except first 7 col

read.count <- featcount %>%
  dplyr::select(all_of(count_cols)) %>%
  as.matrix()

rownames(read.count) <- featcount[[1]] #Add GENES / names

#------------------------ 4.2 SET NAMES & INFO ------------------------#
info <- tibble(old = count_cols) |>
  tidyr::separate_wider_delim(
    old,
    delim = "_",
    names = c("rep", "genotype", "treatment", "rest"),
    too_many = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    genotype_clean = case_when(
      genotype == "ABI" ~ "abi5-7",
      genotype == "LOG" ~ "log2-2",
      genotype == "COL" ~ "COL",
      TRUE ~ genotype
    ),
    new = paste(genotype_clean, treatment, rep, sep = "_")
  )

colnames(read.count) <- info$new
```

# 5. Data Prep
```{r}
#------------------------ 5.1 DESIGN SET UP ------------------------#
sample_names <- colnames(read.count)

# Extract genotype (COL, log2-2, abi5-7)
group_setup <- stringr::str_extract(sample_names, "^(abi5-7|COL|log2-2)")
genotype <- factor(group_setup, levels = c("COL","log2-2","abi5-7"))

# Extract treatment (GM or LEU)
treatment <- stringr::str_extract(sample_names, "(GM|LEU)")
treatment <- factor(treatment, levels = c("GM", "LEU"))

# Build sample info
sample_info <- data.frame(
  row.names = sample_names,
  genotype = genotype,
  treatment = treatment,
  replicate = stringr::str_extract(sample_names, "[0-9]+")
)

# Safety check
stopifnot(all(rownames(sample_info) == colnames(read.count)))

#------------------------ SAVE ------------------------#
#read.count <- tibble::rownames_to_column(as.data.frame(as.matrix(read.count)), "GeneID")
## Convert matrix → data frame with gene IDs
#raw_counts_df <- as.data.frame(read.count)
#raw_counts_df <- tibble::rownames_to_column(raw_counts_df, "GeneID")

#library(writexl)
# Export both CSV and Excel

#writexl::write_xlsx(raw_counts_df, file.path(tables_dir, "LOG2_ABI_raw_counts_clean.xlsx"))
```

# 6. THRESHOLDS, COLORS
```{r THRESHOLDS}
#------------------------ 6.1 Set Values: P.VAL, LFC ------------------------#
pad <- 0.05
lfc_thresh <- 1.0

#------------------------ 6.2 COLORS ------------------------#
colors <- c(
  "COL" = "#1f78b4",   # blue
  "abi5-7" = "#e31a1c",   # red
  "log2-2" = "#33a02c"    # green
)
```

# 7. DESEQ2
```{r DESeq-run, message=FALSE}
#------------------------ 7.1 DESEQ2 MATRIX ------------------------#
dds <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(
  countData = read.count,
  colData = sample_info,
  design = ~ genotype * treatment) #interaction model\ This model answers: 
#baseline differences (LOG2 vs COL, ABI5 vs COL)
#leucine stress effect (LEU vs GM)
#how mutants modify the leucine stress response (interaction terms)

#------------------------ 7.2 Prefilter ------------------------#
keep <- rowSums(counts(dds)) >= 10
dds <- dds[keep, ]

#------------------------ 7.3 RUN DESEQ2 ------------------------#
dds <- DESeq(dds)

#------------------------ 7.4 CHECK ------------------------#
#dds$treatment #check levels
#dds$genotype
#resultsNames(dds)

## Save full DESeq object
#saveRDS(dds, file.path(procdata_dir, "dds_IM_H_UM.rds"))
```

# 8. VST; NORM COUNTS
```{r VST PCA}
#------------------------ 8.1 VST ------------------------#
## Variance stabilizing transformation
#library(ggrepel)

vsd <- vst(dds, blind = FALSE) # blind ignores design
colnames(vsd) <- rownames(sample_info) ## Sample names, match to colData
stopifnot(all(colnames(vsd) == rownames(colData(dds))))  # Check

#------------------------ 8.2 PCA; PLOT ------------------------#
pca_data <- plotPCA(vsd, intgroup = c("genotype","treatment"), returnData = TRUE)
percentVar <- round(100 * attr(pca_data, "percentVar"))

p_pca <- ggplot(pca_data, 
                aes(PC1, PC2, color = genotype, shape = treatment)) +
  geom_point(size = 4.5, stroke = 1.5, alpha = 0.85) +
  scale_color_manual(values = colors, name = "genotype") +
  xlab(paste0("PC1: ", percentVar[1], "% variance")) +
  ylab(paste0("PC2: ", percentVar[2], "% variance")) +
  geom_text_repel(aes(label = name),                 
                  box.padding = 0.35, 
                  max.overlaps = Inf,  # Show all labels
                  size = 3.5, 
                  segment.color = "red",
                  segment.size = 0.3,
                  bg.color = "white", 
                  bg.r = 0.1) +
  labs(title = "Sample Clustering (Variance-Stabilized Counts)",
       subtitle = paste("PC1:", round(percentVar[1],1), "% variance |",
                       "PC2:", round(percentVar[2],1), "% variance")
       ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 13) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", 
        legend.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
        plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold", size = 14),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 12),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
print(p_pca)

#------------------------ SAVE ------------------------#
#ggsave(file.path(graphics_dir, "LOG2_ABI5.png"), 
#       p_pca, width = 12, height = 8, dpi = 300)
```

## BASELINE INTERACTIONS
```{r BASELINE INTERACTIONS}
#------------------------ BASELINE DIFFERENCES; GENOTYPE VS COL ------------------------#
res_LOG2_vs_COL <- results(dds, contrast = c("genotype","log2-2","COL"), alpha = 0.05)
res_ABI5_vs_COL <- results(dds, contrast = c("genotype","abi5-7","COL"), alpha = 0.05)

summary(res_LOG2_vs_COL)
summary(res_ABI5_vs_COL)

#------------------------ THE EFFECT OF III vs. II, UNDER CONDTION A ------------------------#
#This is the effect of “genotype_III_vs_I” minus “genotype_II_vs_I”
#res = results(dds, contrast= c(0,-1,1,0,0,0))

#Genotype differences under GM (the baseline condition)

#LOG2 vs ABI5 under GM:
res_LOG2_vs_ABI5_GM <- results(dds, contrast = c(0, -1, 1, 0, 0, 0), alpha = 0.05)
summary(res_LOG2_vs_ABI5_GM)

#This subtracts:
#LOG2 vs COL
#minus
#ABI5 vs COL
# giving LOG2 vs ABI5 under GM
```

## MAIN TRT EFFECT
```{r MAIN TRT EFFECT}
#------------------------ MAIN TRT EFFECT; LEU vs GM (on COL) ------------------------#
#The condition effect for genotype I (the main effect) Main treatment effect in the reference genotype (COL)
#results(dds, contrast=c("condition","B","A"))

res_LEU_in_COL <- results(dds, contrast = c("treatment", "LEU", "GM"), alpha = 0.05)
#This is the LEU vs GM effect in COL.

summary(res_LEU_in_COL)
```


```{r}
#The condition effect for genotype III.
#This is the main effect plus the interaction term (the extra condition effect in genotype III compared to genotype I).
#Treatment effect in LOG2 (main effect + interaction)
#results(dds, contrast=list(c("condition_B_vs_A","genotypeIII.conditionB")))
#my version:
res_LEU_in_LOG2 <- results(dds,
    contrast = list(c("treatment_LEU_vs_GM", "genotypelog2.2.treatmentLEU")
    ), alpha = 0.05
)
#The condition effect for genotype II.
#This is the main effect plus the interaction term (the extra condition effect in genotype II compared to genotype I).
#res = results(dds, contrast=list( c("condition_B_vs_A","genotypeII.conditionB") ))
#Treatment effect in ABI5 (main effect + interaction)

res_LEU_in_ABI5 <- results(dds,
    contrast = list(c("treatment_LEU_vs_GM", "genotypeabi5.7.treatmentLEU")
    ), alpha = 0.05
)

#This gives the LEU response in ABI5.
summary(res_LEU_in_LOG2)
#This gives the LEU response in LOG2.
#This is to directly compare stress responses across genotypes.
# LEU vs GM in LOG2
summary(res_LEU_in_ABI5)
```

```{r}
#The interaction term for condition effect in genotype III vs genotype I.
#This tests if the condition effect is different in III compared to I
#res = results(dds, name="genotypeIII.conditionB")

#Interaction: does LEU response differ between LOG2 and COL?

res_LOG2_interaction <- results(dds, name = "genotypelog2.2.treatmentLEU")
#This tests:Does LOG2 respond differently to LEU than COL does?
res_ABI5_interaction <- results(dds, name = "genotypeabi5.7.treatmentLEU")
#Interpretation: Positive/negative log2FC here = difference in leucine response in mutant vs COL.These genes would be “stress‑response rewired” by LOG2 or ABI5.
#These are the genes where: LOG2 or ABI5 mutants respond to leucine differently than COL.

summary(res_LOG2_interaction)
summary(res_ABI5_interaction)
```

```{r}
#The interaction term for condition effect in genotype III vs genotype II.
#This tests if the condition effect is different in III compared to II

res_LOG2_vs_ABI5_interaction <- results(dds,
    contrast = list("genotypelog2.2.treatmentLEU", "genotypeabi5.7.treatmentLEU")
)
```

```{r}
plot_ma_and_volcano <- function(res, title){

                  lab = rownames(res),
```

```{r}
#library(pheatmap)
plot_heatmap <- function(res, title, n = 100){

  topgenes <- head(order(res$padj), n)
  mat <- assay(vsd)[topgenes, ]
  mat_z <- t(scale(t(mat)))   # Z-score per gene
  
  # consistent annotation
  ann <- as.data.frame(sample_info)
  rownames(ann) <- colnames(mat_z)
  
  #------------------------ heatmap ------------------------#
HMap<-  pheatmap(
    mat_z,
    show_rownames = FALSE,
    scale = "row",
    cluster_rows = TRUE,
    cluster_cols = TRUE,
    main = title,
    angle_col = 45,
    annotation_col = ann,
    color = colorRampPalette(c("#3B4CC0", "white", "#B40426"))(100),
    fontsize_col = 10,
    border_color = NA,
    silent = TRUE,   # <-- IMPORTANT
    cellwidth = NA,
cellheight = NA,
annotation_names_col = FALSE


  )
  
  return(HMap$gtable)
}
```


```{r}

hmB <- plot_heatmap(res_ABI5_vs_COL, "Baseline: abi5-7 vs COL (GM)")
hmC <- plot_heatmap(res_LOG2_vs_ABI5_GM, "Baseline: log2-2 vs abi5-7 (GM)")
hmD <- plot_heatmap(res_LEU_in_COL, "LEU vs GM in COL")


library(gridExtra)
label_panel <- function(grob, label){
  arrangeGrob(grob, top = textGrob(label, x = 0, hjust = 0,
                                   gp = gpar(fontsize = 14, fontface = "bold")))
}

hmA_l <- label_panel(hmA, "B")
hmB_l <- label_panel(hmB, "C")
hmC_l <- label_panel(hmC, "D")
hmD_l <- label_panel(hmD, "A")


library(gridExtra)
library(grid)
pdf(file.path(graphics_dir, "BASELINE_heatmaps.pdf"), width = 16, height = 12)

grid.arrange(
  arrangeGrob(hmD_l,hmA_l, hmB_l, hmC_l, ncol = 2),
  ncol = 2,
  widths = c(4, 0.6),
  top = textGrob("Transcriptional Differences Across Genotypes and Treatments",
                 gp = gpar(fontsize = 16, fontface = "bold"))
)

dev.off()
```

```{r}
library(clusterProfiler)
library(org.At.tair.db)
## ranked gene list
res_use <- as.data.frame(res_LOG2_vs_COL) %>%
  filter(!is.na(padj))

geneList <- res_use$log2FoldChange
names(geneList) <- rownames(res_use)
geneList <- sort(geneList, decreasing = TRUE)

## Select significant genes
sig_genes <- names(geneList)[which(res_use$padj < 0.05 & abs(res_use$log2FoldChange) > 1)]

## GO enrichment
ego <- enrichGO(
  gene          = sig_genes,
  OrgDb         = org.At.tair.db,
  keyType       = "TAIR",
  ont           = "BP",
  pAdjustMethod = "BH",
  readable      = TRUE
)

dotplot(ego, showCategory = 20)

```
